title: Epoch fence propagation delay led to orphaned variant serves after rollback
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: During a high-throughput rollout swap on 2026-03-01 we observed a delayed propagation of the new route epoch (fence) across orchestrator replicas. The delay allowed an older canary variant to continue servicing a subset of traffic after the controller decided to rollback. This produced split-serving (orphaned variant serves) for ~12 minutes, causing inconsistent responses and increased error rates for some customers using pinned versions. The incident combined a control-plane queueing storm with an edge-side KV cache TTL misalignment and missing cleanup of per-route pin metadata.
timeline: 2026-03-01 09:12 UTC - Canary rollout (variant v2026-03-01-canary) initiated for model 'llama-redwood-13b' (traffic 10%).
2026-03-01 09:28 UTC - Health checks surfaced increased 5xx for canary; automated gate triggered rollback decision but orchestrator reported 'partial apply' for epoch update.
2026-03-01 09:31 UTC - Ops ran manual rollback; controller recorded epoch increment and placed fence=EPOCH_3129 into metadata store.

2026-03-01 09:32 - 09:44 UTC - Under control-plane CPU pressure, fence notifications were slow to reach several router replicas; routers with stale epoch continued routing to canary. Metrics: 12% of requests were still going to canary, error rate for those requests spiked to 18%.

2026-03-01 09:44 UTC - KV cache TTL on sidecar expired and forced a metadata refresh; routers reconciled and orphaned variant serving stopped. Post-incident mitigation applied (emergency epoch fence flush).
root_causes: Orchestrator's fence broadcast path lacks backpressure and retries under transient control-plane saturation; fence messages are best-effort with no guaranteed delivery semantics.
Per-route pin metadata had an infinite or long TTL in the router-side KV cache; cache entries that signaled 'pinned to older variant' prevented immediate reconcile until TTL expiry or manual flush.
No automatic verification step required by the controller to assert that at least 95% of router replicas observed the epoch before declaring rollback complete.
Missing cleanup path for ephemeral rollout pin records when rollback occurs concurrently with metadata broadcast delays.
mitigations_taken: 2026-03-01 10:00 UTC - Emergency job: gated fence re-broadcast to all router replicas; manual cache flush on high-latency regions.
2026-03-01 11:20 UTC - Temporarily increased observability retention and created a dedicated dashboard tile for 'epoch propagation lag' (dashboards/redwood/epoch-lag).
2026-03-02 13:00 UTC - Short-term change: reduce default router-side pin TTL from 15m to 1m and add manual cache-invalidate endpoint for ops.
findings: The orchestrator treats epoch updates as idempotent fire-and-forget; in practice, missing guarantees allow split-brain routing when control-plane load spikes.
Router KV cache semantics were tuned for steady-state efficiency, not rapid rollbacks. Long TTLs improved cost but hurt safety during churn.
Existing rollout runbook assumed eventual consistency; it did not specify a verification gate post-rollback to confirm cluster-wide converge before marking rollout complete.
action_items: AI-1: (ENG) Implement reliable fence delivery: add ack-based broadcast with exponential backoff and per-replica ack tracking. (owner: Marco Ruiz, estimate: 13) - target release: orchestrator-2026.04 - PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/6742

AI-2: (ENG) Add 'converge-check' step for rollbacks: controller must verify >=95% replica epoch match before finishing rollback; fail open only with operator override. (owner: Priya Nair, estimate: 8) - issue: ENG-89112

AI-3: (ENG) Change default router-side pin TTL to 30s, and introduce a sliding TTL on metadata writes to avoid long-lived stale pins. (owner: Marco Ruiz, estimate: 5) - PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/2109

AI-4: (SRE) Add a synthetic alert: 'epoch-propagation-lag > 10s across >5 replicas' and include runbook link. (owner: Liam O'Connor, estimate: 3) - runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Epoch+Propagation+Runbook
AI-5: (QA/ENG) Add integration test that simulates orchestrator saturation and asserts rollback converge semantics under load (owner: QA Team, estimate: 5).

AI-6: (DOCS) Update rollout runbook and incident playbook to include emergency cache flush, converge verification step, and escalation path. (owner: Nora Chen, estimate: 2) - doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Rollout+Runbook
AI-7: (PM) Consider UI safety toggle: require 'converge-check' for all automated rollbacks by default; expose override for power users. (owner: Diego Morales, estimate: 3)
postmortem_notes: We evaluated alternative approaches: stronger consistency on metadata writes (etcd linearizability) vs. acked broadcast. Acked broadcast chosen for lower latency and incremental rollout feasibility.

We intentionally deferred global strongly-consistent metadata to avoid control-plane performance regression for common operations; instead we will provide gating and verification for rollout-critical epochs.

This incident exposed a trade-off between cost (cache TTL) and safety; the short-term TTL change reduces efficiency but is acceptable for rollout safety window. We will revisit after telemetry collection.
next_steps: Owner (Marco Ruiz) to open feature branches for reliable fence broadcast and router TTL change by 2026-03-12.
SRE to add epoch-propagation-lag alert and dashboard by 2026-03-15.
QA to add integration test into CI and a synthetic chaos job simulating control-plane CPU pressure by 2026-03-22.
PM to review UI safety toggle proposal in next planning cycle (2026-W12).
